evidence: Reviewed process image replacement, multithreaded fork/exec, inherited resources, shared memory and IPC.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Device safety, clinical correctness and deployment authorization remain external governed obligations.

evidence: Checked every created process/thread/task/fiber has terminal-state and cleanup ownership.
Checked shared process memory requires synchronization across all execution-context labels.
Checked logical task context never relies on carrier-thread identity under reuse or migration.
Checked blocking paths state whether they suspend logical work or immobilize a carrier.

Checked process separation is never promoted to complete security, safety or availability isolation.
invariant_checking.notes: Exact resource and scheduling invariants must be restated for the chosen OS and runtime versions.

evidence: Reviewed cardinality counterexamples: one worker executes many tasks, a task runs inline, and one runtime context migrates.
Reviewed thread-local trace failure under task migration and worker reuse.
Reviewed all-carriers-pinned calculation as a counterexample to lightweight-context scalability.
Reviewed separate processes sharing files, mappings, credentials or external systems as a counterexample to total isolation.
Reviewed cancellation after database/device commit as a counterexample to cancellation-as-rollback.
Confirmed no scheduler correctness, medical safety or universal performance proof is claimed.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides bounded proofs and falsifying cases, not formal verification of a runtime.

evidence: Audited process, thread, platform, virtual, task, fiber, coroutine, goroutine, blocking, pinned, isolated, parallel, lightweight, safe and scalable claims.

The executable limitation denies real threads, migration, scheduler cost, fairness, visibility, cancellation and production validation.
No external academic, practitioner, clinical, device, safety, security or regulatory review is claimed.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mechanism selection remains evidence-based and runtime-specific.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter separates OS resource/protection domains, kernel execution contexts, logical tasks and runtime resumable contexts, while reserving scheduler implementation, synchronization, event loops, cancellation, structured concurrency, thread pools and task graphs for their dedicated modules.

practitioner_review.notes: Production guidance covers IPC, address-space sharing, worker/task mapping, native blocking and pinning, context propagation, bounded queues, lifecycle, cancellation after effects, fork/exec boundaries, observability, overload, shutdown/restart and high-integrity process isolation.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten examples and five exercises progressing from process and thread identity through pools, migration, fibers, virtual threads, OpenMP tasks and fork to high-stakes isolation and workload-based hybrid selection.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
